title.narrative: Shelter and (NFIs) Interventions for Displaced and Returnees Households in the Gaza Strip

description.narrative: ltpgtThis intervention is an eight-month project (March 15 – November 14, 2025), with a budget of $749,998.06 ,addresses the urgent shelter and NFI needs of 1,500 conflict-affected households (8,400 individuals), comprising 1,000 returnees and 500 internally displaced households (IDPs).ltbrgtFollowing the ceasefire on January 19, 2025, PHC’s Site Management Team assessed shelter needs across Gaza, North Gaza, Khan Younis, and Rafah. The assessment identified severe shelter vulnerabilities, particularly among IDPs in tents and returnees in damaged homes. These households require sealing-off materials, bedding, and essential household items to restore their living conditions and enhance self-reliance. ltbrgtThe project ensures safe, dignified, and habitable living conditions for displaced and returning households through the distribution of: 1,500 Sealing-off Kits (SoKs) – Essential for protecting homes and shelters from weather conditions. 600 Toolkits – To support independent shelter improvements. 500 Framing Kits – Strengthening makeshift structures against harsh weather. 1,210 Bedding Sets – Improving comfort and warmth for vulnerable families. PHC will identify beneficiaries through community service centers, conduct field verification visits, and coordinate with local and international partners to avoid duplication of aid. Distribution will take place at four key points in Gaza City, North Gaza, Khan Younis, and Rafah, ensuring accessibility and efficiency. 20% of supplies will be reserved for emergency cases.ltbrgtThe project integrates protection and gender-sensitive approaches, ensuring priority for female-headed households, persons with disabilities, and the elderly. Additionally, post-distribution monitoring (PDM) will assess impact and beneficiary satisfaction through surveys and field visits.ltbrgtThe project prioritizes vulnerable groups, ensuring safe and accessible distribution points and gender-sensitive implementation. PHC has established complaints and feedback mechanisms (hotlines, email, suggestion boxes) to enhance accountability and transparency. GBV risk mitigation is integrated, with safe spaces for women and targeted support for at-risk populations. ltbrgtThe intervention enhances resilience by equipping households with long-lasting materials and promoting self-reliance. Community involvement ensures local ownership, and PHC’s community hubs will continue supporting affected populations beyond the project period. ltbrgtThis project aligns with the oPt HF 2025 First Reserve Allocation Strategy and the Shelter Cluster priorities, aiming to strengthen humanitarian response capacity, mitigate further displacement risks, and support long-term recovery efforts in Gaza.ltbrgtlt/pgt
